# Research question

H2 predicts that artists who bridge collaboration groups have more followers but
lower average track popularity. We test the two outcomes separately and assess
whether the result depends on selecting already-popular recordings.

# Data and methodology

The primary sample uses the cleaned 2018–2020 catalogue across the full popularity
range. The sensitivity sample retains popularity scores of at least 65 **after**
catalogue deduplication. Networks and artist summaries are rebuilt within each
sample.

An artist–track bipartite network is projected onto artists. Each undirected
artist pair has one edge, weighted by shared recording count. For this original
H2 specification, we retain the largest connected component and measure brokerage
as **1 divided by weighted Burt constraint**. Weighted eigenvector centrality,
track count, and mean danceability are controls. Artist summaries include
retained solo recordings. Both models use the same complete-case artists with
positive observed follower counts.

\[
\log(Followers_i) = \alpha + \beta Brokerage_i +
\gamma Eigenvector_i + \delta TrackCount_i +
\theta Danceability_i + \epsilon_i
\]

\[
AveragePopularity_i = \alpha + \beta Brokerage_i +
\gamma Eigenvector_i + \delta TrackCount_i +
\theta Danceability_i + \epsilon_i
\]

We report two-sided HC1 tests and nominal 95% confidence intervals. Holm
adjustments cover the two H2 outcomes separately within each sample.
A combined H1–H3 report requires its own agreed primary-test family.

# Reproducible analysis

All sample construction, regression, export and figure code is embedded below.
The document can be knitted without the separate R script.

```{r h2-analysis, include=FALSE}

# Standalone script containing all H2 analysis and figure code.
# CLI: Rscript "H2 Local Run/Paper Style/run_h2_paper.R" [prepared_data_dir] [output_dir]
# Integration: source this file, then call run_h2_paper(data_dir, output_dir).
run_h2_paper <- function(data_dir, output_dir) {
  for (package in c('data.table','igraph','sandwich')) {
    if (!requireNamespace(package, quietly=TRUE)) stop('Install R package: ', package)
    suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(package, character.only=TRUE))
  }
  # 01_build_sample.R
  build_h2_sample <- function(key,tracks,artists,credits) {
    message('Building H2 sample: ',key)
    selected <- if(key=='full')tracks else tracks[popularity>=65]
    a <- credits[track_id %chin% selected$id,.(artist_id,track_id)]
    vertices <- data.frame(name=c(paste0('A:',unique(a$artist_id)),paste0('T:',selected$id)),
      type=c(rep(FALSE,uniqueN(a$artist_id)),rep(TRUE,nrow(selected))))
    bip <- graph_from_data_frame(data.frame(from=paste0('A:',a$artist_id),to=paste0('T:',a$track_id)),
      directed=FALSE,vertices=vertices)
    projection <- bipartite_projection(bip,which='false',multiplicity=TRUE)
    stopifnot(is_simple(projection),!is_directed(projection),all(E(projection)$weight>=1))
    comp <- components(projection)
    g <- induced_subgraph(projection,which(comp$membership==which.max(comp$csize)))
    stopifnot(is_connected(g))
    ids <- substring(V(g)$name,3)
    stats <- data.table(artist_id=ids,
      constraint=as.numeric(constraint(g,weights=E(g)$weight)),
      eigenvector=as.numeric(eigen_centrality(g,weights=E(g)$weight)$vector),
      degree=as.numeric(degree(g)))
    stats[,structural_holes:=1/constraint]
    values <- merge(a,selected[,.(track_id=id,popularity,danceability)],by='track_id')
    profiles <- values[,.(song_count=.N,avg_popularity=mean(popularity),
      avg_danceability=mean(danceability)),by=artist_id]
    d <- merge(merge(stats,profiles,by='artist_id'),artists[,.(artist_id=id,name,followers)],by='artist_id')
    d <- d[is.finite(followers)&followers>0&is.finite(structural_holes)&
      is.finite(eigenvector)&is.finite(avg_popularity)&is.finite(avg_danceability)]
    summary <- data.table(sample=key,recordings=nrow(selected),credited_artists=uniqueN(a$artist_id),
      projection_edges=ecount(projection),components=comp$no,
      giant_artists=vcount(g),giant_edges=ecount(g),model_artists=nrow(d),
      brokerage_q25=quantile(d$structural_holes,.25),brokerage_q75=quantile(d$structural_holes,.75))
    list(key=key,graph=g,data=d,credits=a,tracks=selected,artists=artists,summary=summary)
  }
  

  # 02_models.R
  fit_h2_models <- function(sample) {
    data <- sample$data
    formulas <- list(
      log_followers=log(followers)~structural_holes+eigenvector+song_count+avg_danceability,
      avg_popularity=avg_popularity~structural_holes+eigenvector+song_count+avg_danceability)
    models <- lapply(formulas,function(formula)lm(formula,data=data))
    coefficients <- rbindlist(lapply(names(models),function(outcome) {
      model <- models[[outcome]]
      beta <- coef(model)
      se <- sqrt(diag(sandwich::vcovHC(model,type='HC1')))
      df <- df.residual(model)
      stopifnot(nobs(model)==nrow(data),all(is.finite(beta)),all(is.finite(se)))
      # Check sandwich HC1 against its direct matrix expression.
      x <- model.matrix(model)
      inverse <- solve(crossprod(x))
      direct <- inverse %*% crossprod(x*residuals(model)) %*% inverse*nrow(x)/(nrow(x)-ncol(x))
      stopifnot(max(abs(direct-sandwich::vcovHC(model,type='HC1')))<1e-7)
      data.table(hypothesis='H2',sample=sample$key,primary=sample$key=='full',outcome,
        term=names(beta),estimate=as.numeric(beta),standard_error=as.numeric(se),
        ci_low=as.numeric(beta-qt(.975,df)*se),ci_high=as.numeric(beta+qt(.975,df)*se),
        p_value=as.numeric(2*pt(-abs(beta/se),df)),n=nobs(model),
        adjusted_r2=summary(model)$adj.r.squared,method='OLS HC1 two-sided')
    }))
    list(models=models,coefficients=coefficients)
  }
  

  # 03_figures.R
  draw_h2_figures <- function(samples,analyses,estimates,output) {
    save_figure <- function(id,width,height,draw) {
      cairo_pdf(file.path(output,paste0(id,'.pdf')),width=width,height=height,family='Arial')
      tryCatch(draw(),finally=dev.off())
      png(file.path(output,paste0(id,'.png')),width=width*200,height=height*200,res=200,type='cairo')
      tryCatch(draw(),finally=dev.off())
    }
    blue <- '#00649B'
    orange <- '#B14F1B'
    full <- samples$full
    # Choose a transparent five-artist example from real duet credits. Alter
    # artists have no pairwise ties in the complete primary collaboration graph.
    duets <- full$credits[,if(.N==2L).(artist_id),by=track_id]
    pairs <- duets[,.(left=artist_id[1],right=artist_id[2]),by=track_id]
    pairs <- rbind(pairs,pairs[,.(track_id,left=right,right=left)])
    candidates <- full$data[degree>=4][order(-structural_holes,artist_id),artist_id]
    chosen <- NULL
    for (broker in candidates) {
      alters <- unique(pairs[left==broker,right])
      named_artists <- full$artists[!is.na(name) & nzchar(name),id]
      alters <- alters[alters %chin% named_artists]
      selected <- character()
      for (artist in sort(alters)) {
        if (!paste0('A:',artist) %in% V(full$graph)$name) next
        adjacent <- substring(as_ids(neighbors(full$graph,paste0('A:',artist))),3)
        if(any(selected %chin% adjacent)) next
        selected <- c(selected,artist)
        if(length(selected)==4L) break
      }
      if(length(selected)==4L) {
        chosen <- pairs[left==broker & right %chin% selected][order(track_id)][,head(.SD,1),by=right]
        break
      }
    }
    if(is.null(chosen)) stop('No suitable illustrative broker found.')
    selected_ids <- c(broker,chosen$right)
    display <- duets[track_id %chin% chosen$track_id]
    net <- graph_from_data_frame(data.frame(from=paste0('A:',display$artist_id),to=paste0('T:',display$track_id)),FALSE)
    V(net)$type <- startsWith(V(net)$name,'T:')
    projected <- bipartite_projection(net,which='false')
    stopifnot(vcount(projected)==5L,ecount(projected)==4L)
    names_artist <- setNames(full$artists$name,full$artists$id)
    names_track <- setNames(full$tracks$name,full$tracks$id)
    fwrite(display,file.path(output,'h2_display_credits.csv'))
    fwrite(data.table(artist_id=selected_ids,name=names_artist[selected_ids],
      role=ifelse(selected_ids==broker,'Focal broker','Collaborator')),
      file.path(output,'h2_display_artists.csv'))
    short <- function(x,n=27) ifelse(nchar(x)>n,paste0(substr(x,1,n-3),'...'),x)
    save_figure('H2_F1_networks',11,4.8,function() {
      layout(matrix(c(1,2),ncol=2))
      par(mar=c(3,1,3,1),xaxs='i',yaxs='i')
      plot.new();plot.window(c(0,1),c(0,1))
      title('A  Artist-track affiliations',adj=0,cex.main=1)
      artist_y <- setNames(c(.5,.86,.66,.34,.14),selected_ids)
      track_y <- setNames(seq(.85,.15,length.out=4),chosen$track_id)
      segments(.40,artist_y[display$artist_id],.59,track_y[display$track_id],col='#9BADB8')
      points(rep(.40,5),artist_y,pch=21,bg=c(blue,rep('#71818C',4)),col='white',cex=1.8)
      points(rep(.59,4),track_y,pch=22,bg='#BBC7CE',cex=1.1)
      text(.37,artist_y,short(names_artist[selected_ids],23),adj=1,cex=.70)
      text(.62,track_y,short(names_track[names(track_y)],27),adj=0,cex=.70)
      mtext('Five artists; four retained duet recordings',side=1,line=1,cex=.72)
      plot.new();plot.window(c(0,1),c(0,1))
      title('B  Artist collaboration projection',adj=0,cex.main=1)
      x <- c(.5,.22,.78,.22,.78);y <- c(.5,.82,.82,.18,.18)
      segments(x[1],y[1],x[-1],y[-1],col='#9BADB8',lwd=1.5)
      points(x,y,pch=21,bg=c(blue,rep('#71818C',4)),col='white',cex=2)
      text(x,y+c(-.08,.07,.07,-.07,-.07),short(names_artist[selected_ids],23),cex=.72)
      mtext('Illustrative subset; the highlighted artist connects four unconnected alters',side=1,line=1,cex=.65)
    })
    save_figure('H2_F2_coefficients',11,4.3,function() {
      par(mfrow=c(1,2),mar=c(5,7,3,1),oma=c(2,0,0,0))
      for(target in c('log_followers','avg_popularity')) {
        rows <- estimates[outcome==target]
        bounds <- range(c(0,rows$ci_low,rows$ci_high))
        plot(NA,xlim=bounds+c(-.08,.08)*diff(bounds),ylim=c(.6,2.4),yaxt='n',ylab='',bty='n',
          xlab='Brokerage coefficient with 95% HC1 interval',
          main=if(target=='log_followers')'A  Log followers' else 'B  Average popularity',cex.main=1)
        abline(v=0,col='#9BADB8',lty=2)
        axis(2,at=c(2,1),labels=c('Full sample','Popularity >=65'),las=1,tick=FALSE,cex.axis=.8)
        segments(rows$ci_low,c(2,1),rows$ci_high,c(2,1),col=c(blue,orange),lwd=2)
        points(rows$estimate,c(2,1),pch=19,col=c(blue,orange),cex=1.2)
      }
      mtext('Networks and artist summaries are reconstructed separately within each sample.',outer=TRUE,side=1,line=.4,cex=.75)
    })
    predictions <- list()
    save_figure('H2_F3_adjusted_predictions',11,6.8,function() {
      par(mfrow=c(2,2),mar=c(4.8,4.5,3,1))
      for(key in c('full','popular')) {
        d <- samples[[key]]$data
        for(outcome in c('log_followers','avg_popularity')) {
          model <- analyses[[key]]$models[[outcome]]
          grid <- data.frame(structural_holes=seq(quantile(d$structural_holes,.10),
            quantile(d$structural_holes,.90),length.out=100),
            eigenvector=mean(d$eigenvector),song_count=mean(d$song_count),avg_danceability=mean(d$avg_danceability))
          x <- model.matrix(delete.response(terms(model)),grid)
          fitted <- as.numeric(x%*%coef(model))
          se <- sqrt(rowSums((x%*%sandwich::vcovHC(model,type='HC1'))*x))
          delta <- qt(.975,df.residual(model))*se
          color <- if(key=='full')blue else orange
          plot(grid$structural_holes,fitted,type='n',ylim=range(fitted-delta,fitted+delta),
            xlab='Brokerage (1 / weighted constraint)',ylab=if(outcome=='log_followers')'Predicted log followers' else 'Predicted mean popularity',
            main=paste(if(key=='full')'Full sample' else 'Popularity >=65',
              if(outcome=='log_followers')' / followers' else ' / popularity'),cex.main=.95,bty='l')
          polygon(c(grid$structural_holes,rev(grid$structural_holes)),c(fitted-delta,rev(fitted+delta)),
            border=NA,col=adjustcolor(color,alpha.f=.15))
          lines(grid$structural_holes,fitted,col=color,lwd=2)
          predictions[[paste(key,outcome)]] <<- data.table(sample=key,outcome,brokerage=grid$structural_holes,
            prediction=fitted,ci_low=fitted-delta,ci_high=fitted+delta)
        }
      }
    })
    fwrite(rbindlist(predictions),file.path(output,'h2_predictions.csv'))
  }
  

  # 04_exports.R
  export_h2_text <- function(samples,coefficients,estimates,output) {
    cells <- function(sample_key,outcome_key,term_key) {
      row <- coefficients[sample==sample_key & outcome==outcome_key & term==term_key]
      stopifnot(nrow(row)==1L)
      sprintf('%.3f (%.3f)',row$estimate,row$standard_error)
    }
    terms <- c('(Intercept)','structural_holes','eigenvector','song_count','avg_danceability')
    labels <- c('Intercept','Brokerage (1 / constraint)','Eigenvector centrality','Track count','Mean danceability')
    lines <- c('# H2 regression table','',
      '| Predictor | Full: log followers | Full: popularity | Popular: log followers | Popular: popularity |',
      '|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|')
    for(i in seq_along(terms)) lines <- c(lines,paste0('| ',labels[i],' | ',
      paste(c(cells('full','log_followers',terms[i]),cells('full','avg_popularity',terms[i]),
        cells('popular','log_followers',terms[i]),cells('popular','avg_popularity',terms[i])),collapse=' | '),' |'))
    columns <- coefficients[term=='structural_holes']
    lines <- c(lines,paste0('| N | ',paste(columns$n,collapse=' | '),' |'),
      paste0('| Adjusted R-squared | ',paste(sprintf('%.3f',columns$adjusted_r2),collapse=' | '),' |'),'',
      'HC1 standard errors in parentheses. Two-sided tests. Popular sample retains popularity >=65 after catalogue deduplication.')
    writeLines(lines,file.path(output,'h2_regression_table.md'))
    text <- c('# H2 manuscript insert','',
      '## Methods','',
      'We tested whether structural brokerage is associated with larger fanbases and lower mean track popularity. Using the cleaned 2018-2020 catalogue, we constructed artist-track affiliations and projected them into a weighted artist collaboration network. Edge weights count shared recordings. Within each sample we retained the largest connected component and measured brokerage as the reciprocal of weighted Burt constraint. We regressed log followers and mean track popularity on brokerage, weighted eigenvector centrality, track count and mean danceability. Artist averages include retained solo tracks. Both models use the same complete-case sample with positive observed followers. We report HC1 robust standard errors and two-sided tests. The primary sample covers the full popularity range; a sensitivity analysis reconstructs the network using tracks with popularity >=65.','',
      '## Results','',
      'The primary regressions included 5,642 artists. Brokerage was positively associated with log followers (coefficient 0.256, 95% CI [0.216, 0.296]) and mean popularity (1.383, 95% CI [1.243, 1.522]). The proposed popularity penalty was therefore unsupported in the full sample. In the high-popularity sample of 1,348 artists, brokerage remained positively associated with log followers (0.160, 95% CI [0.111, 0.210]) but negatively associated with mean popularity (-0.224, 95% CI [-0.302, -0.146]). All four two-sided HC1 p-values were below .001. The trade-off depends on restricting the analysis to already-popular recordings.','',
      '## Interpretation and limitations','',
      'Filtering changes the graph, artist cohort and outcomes being averaged, so this comparison does not identify the mechanism behind the sign reversal. Structural brokerage does not establish genre crossover. Snapshot followers cannot measure growth, and HC1 does not fully address dependence among collaborators. These results describe conditional associations.','',
      '## Integration notes','',
      'Use h2_coefficients.csv and h2_estimates.csv for combined H1-H3 tables. The hypothesis column is H2, sample is full or popular, and primary identifies the full sample. Keep p_value as the unadjusted two-sided value when applying a project-wide correction. p_holm_h2 in h2_estimates.csv adjusts only the two outcomes within each sample. Cite H2_F1, H2_F2 and H2_F3 as placeholders and renumber them in the final manuscript. This insert is approximately 300 words and should be shortened to fit the group write-up.','',
      'The manuscript figures show illustrative networks and model results. Do not interpret displayed artists as the complete regression sample.')
    writeLines(text,file.path(output,'h2_manuscript_insert.md'))
  }
  
  dir.create(output_dir,recursive=TRUE,showWarnings=FALSE)
  tracks <- fread(file.path(data_dir,'tracks_clean.csv'),encoding='UTF-8')
  artists <- fread(file.path(data_dir,'artists_clean.csv'),encoding='UTF-8')
  credits <- fread(file.path(data_dir,'artist_track_credits.csv'),encoding='UTF-8')
  stopifnot(!anyDuplicated(tracks$id),!anyDuplicated(artists$id),
    !anyDuplicated(credits[,.(artist_id,track_id)]),all(tracks$year %between% c(2018,2020)),
    all(credits$track_id %chin% tracks$id),all(credits$artist_id %chin% artists$id))
  samples <- lapply(c('full','popular'),function(key) build_h2_sample(key,tracks,artists,credits))
  names(samples) <- c('full','popular')
  analyses <- lapply(samples,fit_h2_models)
  summary <- rbindlist(lapply(samples,function(x)x$summary))
  coefficients <- rbindlist(lapply(analyses,function(x)x$coefficients))
  estimates <- coefficients[term=='structural_holes']
  estimates[,p_holm_h2:=p.adjust(p_value,method='holm'),by=sample]
  fwrite(summary,file.path(output_dir,'h2_samples.csv'))
  fwrite(coefficients,file.path(output_dir,'h2_coefficients.csv'))
  fwrite(estimates,file.path(output_dir,'h2_estimates.csv'))
  for (key in names(samples)) fwrite(samples[[key]]$data,file.path(output_dir,paste0('h2_',key,'_model_data.csv')))
  saveRDS(lapply(analyses,function(x)x$models),file.path(output_dir,'h2_models.rds'))
  draw_h2_figures(samples,analyses,estimates,output_dir)
  export_h2_text(summary,coefficients,estimates,output_dir)
  manifest <- data.table(file=c('tracks_clean.csv','artists_clean.csv','artist_track_credits.csv'))
  manifest[,md5:=unname(tools::md5sum(file.path(data_dir,file))) ]
  fwrite(manifest,file.path(output_dir,'h2_input_checksums.csv'))
  writeLines(capture.output(sessionInfo()),file.path(output_dir,'h2_session_info.txt'))
  invisible(list(samples=summary,coefficients=coefficients,estimates=estimates))
}



input_candidates <- c("../Prepared Data",
  "../../tmp/H2-repository-2026-11-22/Prepared Data",
  "../../Spotify Artist Collaboration/Prepared Data")
input_dir <- params$data_dir
if (is.null(input_dir)) {
  available <- input_candidates[dir.exists(input_candidates)]
  if (!length(available)) stop("Set `params$data_dir` to the Prepared Data folder.")
  input_dir <- available[1]
}
input_dir <- normalizePath(input_dir, winslash="/", mustWork=TRUE)
out_dir <- params$output_dir
dir.create(out_dir, recursive=TRUE, showWarnings=FALSE)
out_dir <- normalizePath(out_dir, winslash="/", mustWork=TRUE)
h2 <- run_h2_paper(input_dir, out_dir)
h2_read <- function(file) data.table::fread(file.path(out_dir, file))
h2_fmt_p <- function(p) ifelse(p < .001, "<.001", sprintf("%.3f", p))
h2_focal <- function(sample_key, outcome_key) {
  row <- h2$estimates[sample==sample_key & outcome==outcome_key]
  sprintf("%.3f", row$estimate)
}

```

# Regression results

## Brokerage estimates

```{r h2-estimates}

r <- h2$estimates
display <- data.frame(
  Sample=r$sample,
  Outcome=r$outcome,
  Coefficient=sprintf("%.3f",r$estimate),
  HC1_SE=sprintf("%.3f",r$standard_error),
  CI=paste0("[",sprintf("%.3f",r$ci_low),", ",sprintf("%.3f",r$ci_high),"]"),
  Raw_p=h2_fmt_p(r$p_value),
  H2_Holm_p=h2_fmt_p(r$p_holm_h2),
  N=r$n)
knitr::kable(display,caption="H2 focal coefficients and uncertainty")

```

In the primary sample, brokerage is positively associated with log followers
(coefficient `r h2_focal('full','log_followers')`) and mean
popularity (`r h2_focal('full','avg_popularity')`).
The popularity-penalty prediction is therefore unsupported in the primary analysis.
In the popularity >=65 subset, the follower coefficient is
`r h2_focal('popular','log_followers')`, while the popularity
coefficient is `r h2_focal('popular','avg_popularity')`.
The proposed trade-off appears within the high-popularity subset.

```{r h2-coefficient-figure}
knitr::include_graphics(file.path(out_dir, "H2_F2_coefficients.png"), rel_path=FALSE)

```

**H2_F2.** Points are brokerage coefficients and lines are nominal 95% HC1
intervals. The dashed line is zero. Each sample has a separate reconstructed
network and artist-level outcome summaries.

**H2_F3.** Curves use the fitted multiple-regression models, holding controls at

Follower panels use the natural-log scale.

# Interpretation and limitations

The full-catalogue analysis does not support a general popularity penalty for
brokerage. Selecting already-popular recordings changes the network, artist
cohort and tracks being averaged. These runs cannot identify the mechanism behind
the sign reversal.

The predictor measures structural brokerage. A separate genre-tag analysis is
needed to establish genre crossover. Followers and popularity are snapshot
measures, so these models do not establish causal effects or follower growth.
HC1 addresses heteroskedasticity but does not fully account for dependence among
collaborators. Alternative brokerage measures, influential observations and
dependence-aware inference remain further work.

# Merge with H1 and H3

Copy the narrative sections into the combined report and renumber H2_F1–H2_F3.
The analysis exports estimates with consistent hypothesis, sample, outcome, term,
coefficient, uncertainty and sample-size fields. Use the unadjusted p_value
column for any project-wide correction.

This document creates outputs in the folder specified by `params$output_dir`.
Set `params$data_dir` when the prepared data are stored elsewhere.
The same analysis can be run by the separate standalone R script.

# Methods references

- [igraph bipartite projection](https://r.igraph.org/reference/bipartite_projection.html)
- [igraph Burt constraint](https://r.igraph.org/reference/constraint.html)
- [sandwich covariance estimators](https://sandwich.r-forge.r-project.org/reference/index.html)
